Image watermarks are a way to embed information into a picture, Dr Mike Pound takes us through Adobe's Trust Mark to explain the idea & covers some of the pros and cons. 

00:00 - Introduction: Watermarking Images vs Text
00:28 - Steganography vs Watermarking & Metadata Limitations
01:39 - Why Least Significant Bits (LSB) Fail
04:04 - Deep Learning for Watermarks (Encoder-Decoder)
05:37 - How Do We Detect & Read Embedded Codes?
07:18 - Robust Watermarking: Training with Augmentations
09:21 - Handling Any Image Size (Trustmark & 256px Base)
11:36 - Live Demo: Watermarking an Image in Python
13:40 - Stress Testing: Compression & Resizing
15:48 - Extreme Edits: Cropping & Color Shifts
17:23 - Adversarial Attacks: Copying Watermarks Between Images
19:39 - AI Tracking, Provenance, & Digital Signatures

Computerphile is supported by Jane Street. Learn more about them (and exciting career opportunities) at: https://jane-st.co/computerphile

This video was filmed and edited by Sean Riley.

Computerphile is a sister project to Brady Haran's Numberphile. More at https://www.bradyharanblog.com

snippet.description:
An honest confession by AIR 207 Sugandha Gupta about her UPSC Mains answer writing journey!

Sugandha shares how maintaining daily answer writing consistency was initially difficult, and how she aimed to write answers five to six days a week. She also explains why **writing answers alone is not enough—reviewing your work, analysing topper copies and model answers, learning from fellow aspirants, and rewriting answers are equally important.

If you are preparing for UPSC CSE 2027 or 2028, learn how consistent answer writing and honest self-analysis can help you improve your UPSC Mains preparation.

Write. Analyse. Improve. Repeat.

#SugandhaGupta #AIR207 #upscmains  #answerwriting  #upsc2027  #upscpreparation  #upscstrategy  #levelupias  #shorts
